claim: At d_model=256 (seed 22, m2 fixed at 0.5, data_seed 0, N=128, 6000 steps), N=128 trained force R2 at the best-margin layer is 0.79523 at layer 1 (control 0.65467, margin 0.141, headroom-normalised 0.41). That clears the >= 0.74 prediction and is 0.077 above the d128 value (0.718). However, the gap to the paired d256 N=64 arm could not be computed because run-20261016-050924-d030 is still running. accel_step R2 is 0.91127 at layer 1 (control 0.71358, margin 0.198). Its headroom-normalised margin is 0.69: inside [0.60, 0.90] but 0.18 below the d128 seed-22 value of 0.868, so the 'accel_step stays flat' condition fails.
confidence_note: The force part of expected_if_true happened, and by a wide margin. The deciding criterion did not get tested: the best-layer gap (<= 0.085) and the layer-1 same-layer gap (<= 0.10) both need the paired d256 N=64 arm, which has not finished. If that arm lands near the d64/d128 N=64 values (0.8235 at layer 1, 0.82669 at layer 4), the gap would be about 0.03. That would support a capacity bottleneck, but this is an estimate, not a measurement. The accel_step criterion also fails. The normalised margin fell from 0.868 to 0.69, but the trajectory's max-over-layers accel_step R2 is 0.97 while layer 1 reads 0.911, so the drop may come from higher d256 controls (0.714) or from a different best layer rather than a real loss of decodability. The d128 reference's layer would need checking. Controls rise steeply with width: distance control is 0.916 and energy control 0.912, so both fail the 0.1 bar even though trained R2 is 0.97-0.99. The force control (0.655) is also above the d64 values, which is why the hypothesis compares on trained R2. This is a single seed and a single arm. val_mse_ratio is not monotone (0.28 at step 1500, 0.57 at step 2000), but it ends at 0.0127. The verdict becomes supported if the paired arm gives a best-layer gap <= 0.085 and the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact. It becomes refuted only if the paired N=64 arm comes in at >= 0.895, which is implausible given its d64 and d128 values.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261016-062925-8e31 (issue 0): Accepted. expected_if_true required the d256 N=128 headroom-normalised accel_step margin at the best-margin layer to be within 0.05 of 0.868. The measured value is 0.690 (layer 1, 0.1977/0.2864), so that clause has already failed. I withdraw the statement in the confidence note that the verdict 'becomes supported if ... the accel_step discrepancy turns out to be a layer or control artifact'. That would replace the pre-registered criterion after the fact, the same error accepted on f-20261016-022923-3654 and f-20261016-032946-f8ef. With the paired d256 N=64 arm now complete (run-20261016-050924-d030, force 0.82857 at layer 1), the best-layer gap is 0.82857 - 0.79523 = 0.033. That satisfies the force clause (<= 0.085) but cannot rescue the accel_step clause, so the correct verdict is inconclusive and the status stays inconclusive. The force result should be read only as descriptive: at d256, seed 22's same-layer gap is about 0.033, down from 0.108 at d128 and 0.143 at d64. Any fixed-layer accel_step comparison across widths needs its own pre-registered experiment. The queued seed-23 d256 arms (exp-20261016-054409-a60b/01bd) already describe accel_step without scoring it.
